name: Migrate

hero.title: Keep your React code. Move to Pyreon one screen at a time.
hero.lede: Compatibility layers for React, Preact, Vue, Solid and Svelte cover each framework's public API with near-full parity, so your components run on Pyreon's engine. Then `pyreon check` and a codemod help you rewrite each screen in native Pyreon, where a component runs once.

items.title: Your imports stay
items.text: `pyreon({ compat: 'react' })` points `react`, `react-dom`, `react-dom/client` and the JSX runtime at `@pyreon/react-compat`. The repo's own React example imports from 'react' in 15 files and runs on Pyreon.

items.title: React's rules, kept
items.text: `useState` returns the value, the component body re-runs on change, deps arrays are honoured and closures go stale exactly as they do in React. Code written for that model keeps its meaning.

items.title: Pyreon inside, React outside
items.text: Pyreon's router, query, form, toast and i18n providers ship with the `nativeCompat` marker, so they work inside a compat tree. Mark your own Pyreon helpers the same way and React code can read their context.

items.title: A checklist for the rewrite
items.text: `pyreon check src/` lists the React patterns it finds, each with its line and the Pyreon replacement (“Read: count(), Write: count.set(x)”), and exits non-zero. Burn the list down screen by screen.

difference.title: Same search box. One re-renders on every keystroke.

before.label: React · runs unchanged on react-compat
before.caption: Every keystroke re-runs the whole body; useMemo and its deps array keep the filter from running more than it must. Typechecked and mounted on @pyreon/react-compat as written.

after.label: native Pyreon
after.caption: The body runs once. `query` is a signal and `matches` a computed, so a keystroke updates the count and the list, and nothing else. No deps array to keep in sync.

extraSectionsHtml:
the layers

Five frameworks, one engine.

@pyreon/react-compatReact

41 exports: hooks including use, useActionState and useOptimistic, plus Suspense, lazy, memo, portals; createRoot from /dom. Class components are stubs.

@pyreon/preact-compatPreact

The root, /hooks and /signals entry points. Class components get componentDidMount, componentDidUpdate and componentWillUnmount.

@pyreon/vue-compatVue

The Composition API: ref, reactive, computed, watch, lifecycle, provide/inject, Teleport, KeepAlive, Transition. No .vue compiler.

@pyreon/solid-compatSolid

Signals, stores, resources and For, Show, Switch, Index, Dynamic. Updates are per component, not per node.

@pyreon/svelte-compatSvelte

svelte/store, onMount, onDestroy, tick, context and createEventDispatcher. Not a .svelte compiler.

@pyreon/cli · pyreon checkThe checklist

Lists the React patterns left in each file, with the line and the Pyreon replacement. Exits non-zero, so it gates CI.

@pyreon/mcp · migrate_reactFirst-pass codemod

Rewrites React imports, hook declarations and JSX attributes. Setter calls and reads of the old state you finish by hand; TypeScript flags the dangling setters.

Step by step from React, Vue, Solid, Svelte and Angular, and from React Native to the experimental iOS and Android targets.

groups.name: rewrite tools · pyreon check flags, @pyreon/mcp tools

limits.title: Nested state resets when a parent re-renders
limits.text: In react- and preact-compat a parent re-render rebuilds its subtree, so a child's useState and useRef go back to their initial values and useEffect([]) runs again. memo does not stop it. Lift that state up.

limits.title: Class components
limits.text: React's Component and PureComponent are import-only stubs. preact-compat runs componentDidMount, componentDidUpdate and componentWillUnmount, but has no class error boundaries.

limits.title: No concurrent mode
limits.text: useTransition, useDeferredValue, startTransition and flushSync run synchronously; useLayoutEffect and useInsertionEffect behave like useEffect.

limits.title: No .vue or .svelte compiler
limits.text: vue-compat is the Composition API (no Options API, no templates); svelte-compat covers stores and lifecycle, not rune syntax.

limits.title: Solid and Svelte compat update per component
limits.text: A change re-runs the component, not one DOM node. In svelte-compat, onDestroy also fires when an ancestor re-renders.

limits.title: Some React libraries need their vanilla entry
limits.text: Libraries built on public hooks generally work. zustand/react, heavy react-aria hooks and @xyflow/react do not; use zustand/vanilla or the Pyreon package instead.

limits.title: The codemod is a first pass
limits.text: migrate_react rewrites imports, hook declarations and attributes. Setter calls and reads of the old state stay as written, and a `useRef` becomes a signal, so its `.current` uses need rewriting too. TypeScript flags the dangling setters and arithmetic on a signal; `pyreon check` flags a signal left uncalled in a template string.

limits.title: Dev server needs the next release
limits.text: The published compat packages ship no `jsxDEV`, so `vite dev` renders a blank page; `vite build` is unaffected. The fix is on main and lands in the next release.

comingFrom.title: useState and useEffect
comingFrom.note: No deps array: the effect re-runs when `count` changes because it reads `count()`.

comingFrom.title: ref, computed, watch
comingFrom.note: A signal is read by calling it, not through `.value`. `watch` takes the signal itself as its source.

comingFrom.title: createSignal and Show
comingFrom.note: Closest of the five. Pass `<Show>` the signal (or an accessor) so the condition stays reactive.

comingFrom.title: writable, derived, subscribe
comingFrom.note: `effect` replaces the manual subscribe, and `dispose()` replaces the unsubscribe.

comingFrom.title: signal, computed, effect
comingFrom.note: Same three names. Drop `.value`: call the signal to read it, `.set` or `.update` to write.

recipes.title: Run a React app on Pyreon
recipes.text: Swap the React Vite plugin for Pyreon's. Imports from react and react-dom resolve to the compat layer; for TypeScript, map `react` to the compat package in `paths`, as `examples/react-compat/tsconfig.json` does.

recipes.title: List what's left to rewrite
recipes.text: Real output on a React counter. Each finding says what to write instead, and `--fix` applies the rewrites it marks auto-fixable as a first pass: setter calls stay for you to finish.
recipes.code:
$ pyreon check src/Counter.tsx
  src/Counter.tsx
    1:0  [react:react-import] (auto-fixable — run with --fix)
      Import from 'react' is a React package. Use Pyreon equivalent.
      → import { ... } from "@pyreon/core"
    4:28  [react:use-state] (auto-fixable — run with --fix)
      useState is a React API. In Pyreon, use signal(). Read: count(), Write: count.set(x)
      → count = signal(0)
    5:2  [react:use-effect-deps] (auto-fixable — run with --fix)
      useEffect with dependency array. In Pyreon, effect() auto-tracks dependencies — no array needed.
      → effect(() => {
  // reads are auto-tracked
})
    9:12  [react:class-name-prop] (auto-fixable — run with --fix)
      'className' is a React JSX attribute. Use 'class' in Pyreon (standard HTML).
      → class="counter"

  4 findings in 1 file  ·  some are auto-fixable with --fix
# exit code 1: use it as a pre-commit or CI gate

recipes.title: Use a Pyreon provider from React code
recipes.text: Mark a Pyreon component that calls `provide`, `onMount` or `effect` with `nativeCompat`, and React components below it read its context through their own `useContext`.

faq.q: Will my app behave exactly as it does on React?
faq.a: No. It is near-full parity with each framework's public API, and each package's README lists where it differs: nested state across parent re-renders, class components, concurrent mode, layout-effect timing.

Libraries that only use public hooks (useState, useEffect, useReducer, useMemo, useRef) generally do. Libraries that reach into React internals or its scheduler, such as zustand/react, do not; their vanilla entry points do.

faq.q: Is a compat app as fast as native Pyreon?
faq.a: We publish no compat benchmark. A compat component re-runs its body on every state change, in the Vue, Solid and Svelte layers too, where the real frameworks update finer than that; a native Pyreon component runs once. The numbers elsewhere on this site are for native Pyreon.

On a React counter it turned useState into signal, useEffect into effect, className into class and removed the React import. It left `setCount(count + 1)` and the reads of `count` as written, so the file needs those finished by hand before it runs; TypeScript reports `setCount` as undefined.

faq.q: Can I mix native Pyreon components into a compat app?
faq.a: Yes. Pyreon's own providers are marked already; mark your own with `nativeCompat` when they call provide, onMount or effect.
No. The Vue and Svelte layers cover what your code imports. Single-file components need their own compiler.
